prompted_by: the owner's doubt: 'are we sure? i think were getting smth wrong'

error_1.claim: the 27-VEV route PROVABLY STOPS ONE STEP SHORT of the SM
error_1.what_is_true: 27 -> 10+5+5bar+5bar+1+1 under SU(5) contains no 24; 27 VEVs alone cannot break SU(5) -> SM
error_1.what_was_wrong: the SCOPE. The 78 (adjoint) of E6 contains a 24 -- 78 -> 45+16+16bar+1 under SO(10), and 45 -> 24+10+10bar+1 under SU(5) -- so SU(5) -> SM is broken by an ADJOINT VEV, which E6 obviously has. The standard chain uses BOTH: 78 VEVs for the rank-PRESERVING steps, 27 VEVs for the rank-REDUCING one. 'Stops one step short' is true only for 27-ONLY breaking -- the E6SSM's restriction, which exists because string constructions often supply only 27s. It is NOT a statement about the VEV route in general.
error_1.severity: scope error -- the quoted branching fact stands, the inference does not

error_2.banked_where: B952, B959, B960, and echoed in B962
error_2.claim: the object does not supply a VEV
error_2.what_was_wrong: FALSE. The unbroken group after an adjoint VEV <Phi> is the STABILIZER of <Phi> under the adjoint action -- i.e. the CENTRALIZER of <Phi>. So 'adjoint VEV' and 'measurement / centralizer' are THE SAME OPERATION. The object DOES supply VEVs: the adjoint ones. That IS the measurement cascade.
error_2.severity: substantive -- a repeatedly banked framing is wrong

the_corrected_picture.object_supplies: the rank-PRESERVING (adjoint) VEVs -- this IS the measurement cascade
the_corrected_picture.why_B952_still_stands: adjoint VEVs preserve rank, which is exactly why the cascade is rank-preserving; B952's obstruction is UNCHANGED and now has a physical name
